item.title: Changing how you think about time could help you accomplish year-end goals: Q&A
item.description: The way time is described can shape everything from our motivation to our decision-making, according to new research from behavioral scientist Dr. Deepak Sirwani, an assistant professor at the UBC Sauder School of Business. The study is published in the Journal of Marketing Research. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Transferable chemical prediction approach may help reduce trial and error
item.description: Chemical predictions can help prevent unwanted reactions or improve the efficacy of industrial processes, among other applications, but predicting how chemicals interact can be costly and time-consuming—especially because chemicals may behave differently from one environment to another. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Resistance to change has 12 different drivers, new measurement tool reveals
item.description: Almost all change is difficult: adapting your lifestyle, a reorganization at work, or starting to use gender-neutral language. When behavioral change is required, resistance is therefore often encountered. As a result, it can sometimes take a long time for a change to be accepted—and sometimes it doesn't happen at all. It is therefore important to understand where that resistance comes from, according to Radboud University communication scientist Marieke Fransen. Fransen and her colleagues investigated this and identified 12 reasons. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Blue Origin is going all in on the New Glenn rocket
item.description: The infrastructure is designed to support multiple flights per week by the end of the decade. Fuente: Ars Technica.
item.dc:creator: Eric Berger

item.title: UN chief says ‘subsidising fossil fuels is subsidising suicide’
item.description: The United Nations says that for every dollar invested in protecting or restoring nature, about $30 still goes into activities that degrade it. Fuente: The Hindu - International.

item.title: Winter sea ice loss may be underestimated, ancient clues from a warmer Arctic suggest
item.description: Future Arctic winter sea ice is likely to shrink by around 1 million square kilometers (386,000 square miles) more than previously thought, after researchers used clues from a warm period 6,000 years ago to improve the reliability of climate models. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: Image: This image over part of West Antarctica was captured by Copernicus Sentinel-3 on 30 September 2026. Fuente: European Space Agency.

item.description: All those Commando war stories I read. Sudeep Sarkar Fuente: National Geographic.

item.title: Performance under pressure: A new perspective on why we fail—or rise to the occasion
item.description: The decisive penalty kick in a final, match point in tennis or the last attempt in a competition: When a lot is at stake, even a well-practiced performance can suddenly break down. Yet pressure does not necessarily impair performance. Some people perform at their best precisely in the moments that matter most. Existing accounts can only partly explain why. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: PLATO, el telescopio europeo con 26 ojos que quiere encontrar por fin una segunda Tierra
item.description: Desde que comenzaron a buscarse exoplanetas en 1992, se han documentado más de 6.000 , de los cuales apenas un centenar pueden considerarse similares a la Tierra. Cuando hablamos de planetas parecidos al nuestro, normalmente nos referimos a su morfología rocosa o al tamaño, no demasiado alejado del terrestre. Sin embargo, si nos proponemos buscar una Tierra 2, sería ideal que su órbita sea más o menos de un año. Es decir, que tarde en girar alrededor de su estrella el mismo tiempo que tarda la Tierra en dar una vuelta completa al Sol. Eso es más difícil de encontrar con los telescopios… Fuente: Xataka.
item.dc:creator: Azucena Martín

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. To view this […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: First in-depth map of 'forever chemicals' in the Finger Lakes created
item.description: In 2023, professor Damian Helbling was getting a lot of calls and emails from local residents. The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) had just announced regulations to limit per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS)—some of which have been linked to cancers and other negative health effects—in drinking water. Ithacans and others in the region wanted to know about levels in the ponds, lakes, streams and creeks in their proverbial backyards. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Endangered species in Canada face extensive delays receiving protection
item.description: For more than 20 years, Canada's Species at Risk Act (SARA) has protected wildlife that are at risk of being lost from Canadian lands and waters. Once a species is listed as extirpated, endangered or threatened under the act, it becomes illegal to kill, harm or capture it or damage its residences. Its critical habitat must also be protected, at least on federal land. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: A rare family of barn owls moved into Manhattan's Upper West Side. New Yorkers are captivated
item.description: Manhattan's Upper West Side has been reveling in the company of its latest celebrities: A family of barn owls nested in a water tower atop a building near Central Park. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Can extra weight weigh on your dog's brain?
item.description: Scientists have learned a lot about what happens to the human body as we age. But there's still much to learn about how other species age, including dogs. Even carrying extra weight could affect a dog's cognitive health. Alexandra Genualdi, a student at Oklahoma State University who presented her research in September at the American Physiological Society's 2026 Comparative Physiology conference in Orlando, talks about her efforts to learn more. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: "Yo te daré nietos": familias israelíes usan el esperma póstumo de sus hijos para tener descendencia
item.description: A raíz del ataque de Hamás de 2023, una norma temporal de emergencia facilita que padres, pero también parejas, extraigan el semen de los cadáveres de sus seres queridos sin una orden judicial. El uso del material genético aún requiere el permiso de los tribunales de familia. No obstante, lo que antes era una práctica casi anecdótica, hoy se ha convertido en política de Estado y, en tres años, 21 civiles y 250 soldados muertos han pasado por este proceso. Fuente: France 24 - Español.
item.dc:creator: Janira Gómez Muñoz

item.title: In animated films, nonhuman characters are still overwhelmingly male
item.description: Female protagonists in animated films have come a long way over the past several decades. Take the 1959 movie "Sleeping Beauty": Soft-spoken and vulnerable, Princess Aurora is cursed as an infant by the evil fairy Maleficent and ultimately saved not by her own wits, but by a prince's kiss. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: The pianist who never played
item.description: Nature, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03112-0 A note to self. Fuente: Nature.

item.description: Nature, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-03253-2 US PhD graduates who used artificial intelligence were more likely to work in industry. Fuente: Nature.
item.dc:creator: Mohana Basu

item.title: Newly discovered viruses reveal an evolutionary missing link
item.description: Researchers at the University of Miami have identified a group of previously unknown viruses that bridge an evolutionary gap between viruses and cellular protein compartments, a discovery with implications for both biotechnology and scientists' understanding of the origins of life. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Rigorous analysis confirms NASA's Artemis II heat shield performance
item.description: NASA’s Artemis II mission sent four astronauts around the Moon and brought them safely back to Earth, laying a foundation for crewed flights to the Moon’s surface. Additional engineering data analysis of the Orion spacecraft’s heat shield confirmed initial data showing the heat shield performed as expected. In particular, NASA measured whether the thermal protection […] Publicado también por: NASA. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: White Sands footprints suggest humans experienced abrupt environmental shifts during the last ice age
item.description: Expanded excavations at White Sands National Park in New Mexico have provided researchers an opportunity to refine the age of the oldest human footprints in North America and establish a deeper understanding of the landscape and environmental conditions at the time humans were present there. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Imperial woodpecker returns to life as a detailed digital specimen
item.description: Researchers have created a detailed, animated 3D model of the imperial woodpecker (Campephilus imperialis), a spectacular bird that has not been confirmed in the wild since 1956. The model, built from a museum specimen and the only known film footage of the living bird, is freely available to scientists, educators and the public. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Food, fear and physics help explain group behavior from plankton to whales
item.description: The open ocean is a dynamic environment, where food is patchy, predators are plentiful, and oceanographic conditions change constantly. Life in the pelagic environment—the offshore waters that extend from the sunlit surface through the twilight zone—requires unique adaptations for survival. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New spectroscopy method enables direct comparisons of nuclear sizes across heavy elements
item.description: The size of a nucleus (nuclear charge radius) is an important physical quantity that reflects the arrangement of protons and neutrons within the nucleus. Particularly in deformed nuclei, such as those of rare-earth elements, examining changes in the charge radius can deepen our understanding of nuclear structure and nuclear deformation. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Cristina Koch, astronauta de Artemis II, de 47 años: “Para explorar el universo y otros planetas, primero debemos entender cómo cuidar el nuestro”
item.description: Luego de completar con éxito el histórico sobrevuelo lunar, se conoció una frase que pronunció mientras realizaba la misión; dejó de ser astronauta en activo tras ser nombrada recientemente como subeditora de ingeniería de la NASA Fuente: La Nación - El Mundo.

item.title: Lunar fault maps reveal how much the moon is shrinking
item.description: A new study of young tectonic landforms on the moon offers the most detailed estimate yet of how much the moon has contracted as its interior gradually cooled over time. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Nearly half of reef-building coral species face higher risk of extinction
item.description: A University of Portsmouth scientist has helped lead a major global study, which finds that 44% of the world's reef-building coral species are now threatened with extinction—and warns the true figure is likely to be even higher. Publicado también por: Nature. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: African American young adults favor family support when it comes to caring for older adults
item.description: A study led by Nekehia Quashie, an assistant professor of public health in the University of Rhode Island's College of Health Sciences, examined how different African American age groups felt about the responsibility of supporting older adults. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: First bacterial galactose oxidase expands toolkit for greener drug and food ingredient production
item.description: To produce pharmaceuticals, food ingredients, and flavors and fragrances, it is often necessary to oxidize alcohols. In conventional chemistry, this transformation typically relies on harsh oxidants and elevated temperatures and generates toxic waste. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Washington captures record 2.16 million invasive green crabs, but experts warn invasion is far from over
item.description: Washington state removed more than 2.16 million invasive European green crabs during fiscal year 2025-26. First detected in the state in 2016, the species threatens native marine life, including clams, oysters and eelgrass. Despite more than $8 million in state funding, no established populations have been eradicated, and researchers warn the invasion could worsen. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Electron density check offers better starting point for chemistry's most difficult metal molecules
item.description: New materials and catalysts have the potential to transform everything from food production and medicine to batteries and stainless steel. Computer simulations help scientists narrow down promising candidates before testing them in a lab, but those simulations can be unreliable, especially for molecules that contain multiple metals. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Beyond national parks: Researchers explore a broader future for conservation
item.description: As governments prepare to gather in Armenia for the U.N. biodiversity summit, researchers are highlighting a conservation approach that recognizes places where nature thrives beyond conventional protected areas. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Measuring deep-ocean oxygen with microscopic magnetic fossils
item.description: Humanity's ongoing disruption of atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO₂) concentrations, temperatures, and global nutrient cycles is starving the oceans of oxygen. Although we can measure ongoing changes to ocean circulation and marine life, we still don't know how far the oxygen loss and the damage to ocean ecosystems could go. One way to foresee the oceans' future is to look back at how our seas and their inhabitants responded to higher CO₂ levels and warmer climates in the past. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Retail research shifted in five ways, study finds
item.description: Retail research has changed during the last couple of decades, according to an analysis of almost 5,200 papers covering business practices, consumer behavior and technology. The study, published in the International Journal of Electronic Marketing and Retailing, considered papers from the four leading specialist journals in this area. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Baby lobster decline foreshadows major midcoast population losses, study shows
item.description: A steep drop in baby lobsters provided an early warning of the sharp decline in adult lobsters along Maine's midcoast, a new University of Maine study shows. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Building trust in governments through digital platforms
item.description: Around the world, many people report distrusting their government. In some places, such as Latin America, North America and Africa, trust in government has declined in recent decades. How can governments rebuild this trust? Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Molecular snapshots reveal how viral enzymes switch between inserting and removing DNA
item.description: Bacteriophages, or viruses that infect bacteria, have a fiendishly simple purpose in life: attach to a bacterial cell, inject their DNA and then use the host's genetic machinery to reproduce. In doing so, they may have evolved some of the most efficient gene-editing tools ever seen in nature. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Single 2D crystal transforms into transistor with built-in insulation and electrical contacts
item.description: A transistor normally requires several fundamentally different materials—a semiconductor to carry current, an insulating dielectric to control it and metallic contacts through which current enters and leaves. Integrating all of these components becomes increasingly difficult as semiconductor devices approach the atomic scale. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Targeting the cell cycle for cancer therapy: From the discovery of CDK9 to precision medicine and beyond
item.description: More than 30 years after the direct connection was established between the molecular machinery controlling cell division and cancer, a new paper traces the evolution of cyclin-dependent kinase research and outlines the next generation of CDK-targeted therapies. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Denis Villeneuve Chose to Direct New James Bond Movie After ‘Dune 3’ Because ‘I Need a Powerful Rocket to Pull Me Away From Arrakis’
item.description: Denis Villeneuve recently told Empire that he returned to “Dune” for a third and final chapter so he can be “severe with the material,” and that his upcoming James Bond movie will be the “very powerful rocket” he needs to “pull me away from Arrakis.” “I said, ‘Maybe it’s a good idea to go back […] Fuente: Variety.
item.dc:creator: Jack Dunn

item.title: The little‑known 14th-century battle that has shaped English, Scottish and French relations
item.description: On Oct. 17, 1346, the Battle of Neville's Cross was fought outside Durham in the northeast of England. It was a decisive moment in Anglo-Scottish history that led to the capture of King David II of Scotland. Yet few have heard of it. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: North Sea heat wave fueled underwater plankton bloom largely missed by satellites
item.description: When a marine heat wave strikes, scientists often turn to satellites to see how the ocean is responding. From space, changes in ocean color can reveal shifts in phytoplankton, microscopic organisms that form the foundation of marine food webs and play a crucial role in the global carbon cycle. But satellites have a fundamental limitation: they can only see the ocean's surface. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Six lessons to improve leadership opportunities for women with disability
item.description: Employers must do more to remove the barriers preventing women with disability from progressing into leadership, according to a new report from People with Disability Australia (PWDA), the national disability rights and advocacy organization. Researchers identify six lessons to help drive change. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA to Help Unlock Mysteries of Mars’ Moons in Upcoming Mission
item.description: NASA is playing an important role in JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) mission, to advance our understanding of Mars’ moons and build on the agency’s long history of exploring the Red Planet. The mission aims to characterize and determine the origin of Mars’ moons Phobos and Deimos and deliver a sample […] Fuente: NASA.

item.title: Donald Trump 'openly financing Russia's war with Ukraine', Nobel peace laureate says
item.description: Speaking with FRANCE 24's Mark Owen, Nobel Peace laureate Oleksandra Matviichuk, Director of the Centre for Civil Liberties, says that with the diesel-supply deal with Moscow Donald Trump "is openly financing this war, by lifting sanctions is providing Russia with opportunities to earn more money" adding that "extra money will be converted in rockets and drones and additional deaths among the civilian population". Fuente: France 24 - English.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Two brain circuits coordinate fruit flies' wing and leg movements to threaten rivals
item.description: Limbs evolved as a means of locomotion. From the primitive rotating flagella of bacteria to the wings of flies and even our own legs, animals use these appendages to travel to find food or mates or escape predators. But in countless species across the animal kingdom, limbs are repurposed to create elaborate social displays: Birds of paradise fan out their wings and hop around in courtship dances, while crabs wave their claws to communicate to potential mating partners. As humans, we use our limbs to dance, gesture while talking, wield tools and conduct a remarkable diversity of behaviors. How… Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How did Mars get its moons? Japan's MMX space mission aims to solve the puzzle
item.description: The Earth got its moon when a small planet collided with our planet more than 4 billion years ago. This impact hurled molten rock into space, which eventually coalesced to form the satellite we can see every night from across our planet. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Keeping up with a pack of hunting wolves is just another day at the office for Bertie Gregory and his team.... Ver más

item.title: Scientists make cells from an 80-year-old donor appear young, advancing ageing research
item.description: Scientists have reprogrammed blood-cell precursors from an 80-year-old donor into neural stem cells with an epigenetic age below 20, according to a study published in Aging Cell. The process unfolded gradually over more than 100 days, offering researchers a way to investigate cellular rejuvenation and its potential implications for ageing and Alzheimer's research. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: John Lennon and Yoko Ono’s Palm Beach mansion rises from $725,000 to $36 million
item.description: El Solano, a captivating mansion nestled in Palm Beach, was acquired by music legend John Lennon and his partner Yoko Ono in 1980. Following Lennon’s untimely passing, Yoko executed extensive renovations before offloading the property in 1986. The illustrious estate changed hands several times, skyrocketing in value, and ultimately fetched $36 million in 2020. Today, it stands as a cherished landmark, intertwining Lennon’s artistic legacy with architectural history. Fuente: The Times of India - World.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Researchers find that some weeds get supercharged by an indirect hit of herbicide
item.description: A brush with low doses of the herbicide dicamba spurs oxalis, a weed commonly known as wood sorrel, to produce more flowers, University of Michigan researchers have discovered. The finding suggests that farmers and homeowners are inadvertently making weeds growing around the perimeter of their fields or lawns stronger, the researchers say. The study results are published in the journal New Phytologist. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Better together? Coral fusion could throw bleached reefs a lifeline
item.description: When corals are stressed by pollution, high water temperatures or other environmental changes, they can lose the microscopic algae living inside them and on which they depend for food. As a result, they turn white, a phenomenon known as coral bleaching. They will not die straight away, but it will be game over if the stress continues long enough for them to starve. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Anthropic is letting METR researchers look under the hood with employee-level access
item.description: METR will publish its own assessments of Anthropic’s risks, incidents, and practices, and the frontier AI model maker has given up the right to block them. Fuente: TechCrunch.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Mehta

item.title: What did the Liberty Bell sound like? Science is on the case.
item.description: Researchers hunted for clues in modal analysis of 20th-century replica bell at Penn State Behrend. Fuente: Ars Technica.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Ouellette

item.title: Lion tracks from the ice age: How two ways of seeing brought ancient animals to life
item.description: The coastline near the southern tip of Africa looked vastly different between about 400,000 years ago and 70,000 years ago, compared with today. At times it lay as much as 100km (62 miles) south of its present location, exposing the vast Palaeo-Agulhas Plain, which contained an extensive habitat for large mammals. At other times the sea level was briefly as much as 13 meters (43 feet) higher than today's mean level. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New DNA sequencing methods detect rare mutations acquired as bodies grow and age
item.description: Somatic mutations, the DNA changes that occur as our bodies grow and age, not only hold an important key to cancer but are emerging as the seeds of a wide range of common, noncancerous diseases. The Somatic Mosaicism across Human Tissues (SMaHT) Network, a National Institutes of Health Common Fund initiative to catalog all the normal processes of somatic mutation, has published its first comprehensive benchmarking study in the journal Cell. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: How COVID reshaped college grading
item.description: Twenty-three Indiana University undergraduates are co-authors on a new study examining how the pandemic reshaped college grading, the result of a semester-long research seminar that took them from a classroom question to a published paper in a national academic journal. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Nearly 600 California earthquakes help validate models that forecast next-day seismic risk
item.description: The University of Bristol–led study, published in Nature Communications, could help millions of people living in earthquake-prone countries make better-informed decisions about seismic risk, particularly during ongoing periods of increased earthquake activity. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Neanderthals capable of both violence and care, bones from Iraqi cave suggest
item.description: Neanderthals were not the unintelligent cave dwellers of popular imagination, but may have been capable of showing both violence and care, researchers who have discovered bones dating back 75,000 years have said. Fuente: Sky News - World.

item.title: El Niño a 'terrifying' threat to coral reefs: UN biodiversity expert
item.description: A super El Niño fueling record ocean temperatures poses a "terrifying" threat to the world's fragile coral reefs, the chair of the U.N.'s expert nature panel told AFP. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Plants use a molecular measuring tape to tell fungal friend from foe
item.description: Chitin, a chain of repeating sugar molecules, is the main building block of fungal cell walls. When fungi grow or are broken down, fragments of chitin chains of different lengths end up in the soil, and plants detect them to monitor the microbes around them. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Study reveals how young adults' work lives affect their parents' mental health
item.description: Earlier this fall, researchers Sara Kalucza (Department of Sociology) and Anna Baranowska-Rataj (Center for Demographic and Aging Research, CEDAR) at Umeå University published a research article showing a connection between young people's school-to-work transitions and parental health. The research used data from CEDAR's demographic database. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: In plants, sense of time is connected with sense of danger
item.description: Salty soil is a growing threat to crops worldwide. Hotter, drier weather has increased evaporation rates, drawing moisture from the soil and leaving behind concentrated mineral salts. At the same time, water shortages are forcing farmers to irrigate using water from lower-quality, saline or recycled sources. Scientists estimate that around half of the world's irrigated farmland is now affected by salinity to some degree. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: El Departamento de Justicia suspende el intercambio de pruebas con los investigadores de los tiroteos mortales de ICE
item.description: El Departamento de Justicia suspende el intercambio de pruebas con los investigadores de los tiroteos mortales de ICE CNNESPANOL.CNN.COM El Departamento de Justicia suspende el intercambio de pruebas con los investigadores de los tiroteos mortales de ICE | CNN Fuente: CNN en Español.

item.title: Global ice-cliff survey tests disputed theory behind projections of accelerated sea level rise
item.description: A new study led by the Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (WHOI) provides the most comprehensive observational analysis yet of the towering ice cliffs that fringe Earth's ice sheets, giving scientists new evidence to evaluate a long-debated process that could influence future sea level rise. Improving these projections is increasingly important as rising seas threaten coastal communities and infrastructure worldwide. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: I discovered a Roman fort in Wales—it may hold the key to the ancient Welsh legend of Macsen Wledig
item.description: My recent discovery of a Roman fort and its extraordinary connection with medieval folklore was the fruition of many hours of painstaking research. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Wild birds rewrite rules of flight efficiency: Study reveals power of 'free fuel' from the sky
item.description: An international study has overturned a longstanding textbook view of how much energy animals use to travel, revealing that flying can sometimes be cheaper than swimming. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: NASA Satellites Observe Historic 2026 El Niño

item.title: India's cobras share genetic ties across the mainland, while Sri Lankan cobras form a distinct genetic lineage
item.description: The spectacled cobra (Naja naja) is one of India's "big four" snakes responsible for most serious snakebite cases. It is currently considered one species, which lives across much of South Asia, with regional differences in color, hood markings and venom. However, it's still unclear which regional cobra populations represent separate evolutionary groups. A new study published in Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution has helped parse out which groups have different lineages, and when and where they may have diverged from their ancestors. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Quantum calculations reveal how spin defects lose energy
item.description: When light hits a tiny defect embedded in a solid material like diamond or silicon carbide, it can kick the defect's electrons into an excited state. These spin defects have the potential to be used as stable, readable qubits for quantum technologies, for example, quantum sensing. But modeling the full physics of their energetics over time—a key step in developing spin defects into new technologies—is a challenging task. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: Solving the mystery behind a flightless beetle's transatlantic journey
item.description: They can't fly or swim, so why do their closest relatives appear on different continents? Grey Gustafson, an associate professor in the Department of Biological Sciences, discovered through DNA sequencing that the ancestors of some of today's tiger beetles existed in South America and Africa before the two continents separated. What's more, North America's largest tiger beetles are related to these ancestral South American giant tiger beetles. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.title: New smart patch could help detect and treat blood clots after spinal surgery
item.description: Blood clots that develop after spinal surgery can lead to serious complications. When blood accumulates around the spinal cord, it may increase pressure on surrounding nerves, potentially causing severe pain, muscle weakness or even paralysis. Early detection and timely treatment are therefore essential. However, continuously monitoring these complications remains challenging, and conventional treatments may require additional surgery. Fuente: Phys.org.
